messages:
miguel: Quick FYI — I deployed a small routing tweak to prefer `eu-lowlat` for short requests (<100 tokens). Aimed at shaving p99 for tiny chat completions. Rollout set to 5% but see notes below.
elaine: link? PR/commit? :eyes:
miguel: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/r1234 commit 9f2b. config excerpt below. I left a rollback flag and a canary tag.
```json
{"route_match": {"path_prefix": "/v1/generate", "max_input_tokens": 100}, "routing": [{"pool": "eu-lowlat", "weight": 70}, {"pool": "shared", "weight": 30}], "canary": {"percent": 5, "gate": "tag:canary-small-requests"}, "fallback":"shared"}
```
khari: Uh — we need to be careful about header overrides. Some clients set `X-Region-Preference` and we currently honor header-first. That can cause the canary percent to spike for those keys.
miguel: Yup spotted that. The rollout rule is global but header precedence can route entire API keys into the lowlat pool. I limited API-key affinity in the canary gate but not the header path.
elaine: Suggestion — add a per-key reservoir cap + sample-by-token approach. For example, cap to 0.5% per API key when canary active. That prevents a single power-user from skewing telemetry.
nina: Also telemetry: our current sampling is uniform over requests; because short requests are more likely small completions, our metric set will be biased. We should emit both sampled and deterministic counters: sampledLatency and fullCounter for p50/p95 computed from all requests that hit the evaluation hook.
oncall-bot: incidenting: no alerts triggered. monitoring: rollout_metric.canary_weight=5%
khari: UX question — Console shows canary percent but doesn't show per-key caps or header stickiness. Product asked for better visibility before full rollout. We should add a per-route breakdown card in Console (by API-key, by header, by region pool).
miguel: Agreed. For immediate safety: I added a guard in the routing layer to ignore `X-Region-Preference` for any request when `canary.tag==canary-small-requests` unless the request is explicitly whitelisted. Patch:
```diff
- prefer header if present
+ prefer header only if whitelist.contains(api_key) || !canary_active
```
That keeps header overrides for known partners but protects the canary.
elaine: Good short-term. But long-term we need deterministic sampling that composes with header-based overrides and session affinity. Prefer: sample by hashed(api_key+path+seed) with fallback to per-request random when anonymous. That way we get reproducible cohorts.
nina: Telemetry hook: add a tag `sampling_context` with values ["deterministic","header-forced","whitelist"] so dashboards can filter. Also emit `cohort_hash` to join logs with tracing.
miguel: Implemented provisional metrics: `canary_exposed_count`, `canary_by_key_count`, `canary_header_overrides`. Pushed to metrics registry behind feature flag.
khari: One more edge: quota enforcement after routing. If the canary pool has separate quotas, header-forced clients might exceed intended rate limits. Confirmed with infra — quotas are applied per-pool post-route.
elaine: We should ensure quota checks run before any expensive model allocations — ideally in the gateway before KV cache warming. If quota denies, route should not be counted in canary metrics — otherwise we inflate canary success rates.
nina: Agreed — add `route_counted_in_canary` boolean to the event only when quota_check.passed and routing.selected_pool==canary_pool.
miguel: Ok — I'll patch the gateway: (1) pre-route quota check, (2) header whitelist guard, (3) per-key reservoir cap at 0.5% overrideable via admin. Rolling out to 5% canary now but will watch `canary_by_key_count` closely.
elaine: For Console work: I'll open a tiny card to show per-route breakdown and sampling_context. We can iterate.
khari: Thanks. If we see any p99 spike or unexpected cost delta, revert to shared pool and set canary to 0% — please notify #eng-oncall and page if p99 > 2x baseline.
oncall-bot: note: adding oncall paging rule for canary p99 threshold > baseline*2
miguel: Noted. Will monitor dashboards and post updates here. :thumbsup:
